title: Highest temperature in London on September 4?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for London's highest temperature on September 4, 2026, centers on 21–23°C, reflecting model consensus for a cooler, fresher day after warmer conditions on the 3rd.**

Official guidance from the Met Office and BBC Weather highlights an incoming Atlantic weather front bringing increased cloud cover, patchy drizzle or light rain, and moderate westerly winds that limit daytime heating. This synoptic setup favors maximum temperatures several degrees below the prior day's potential peaks near 27°C, with reduced solar insolation and advection of cooler maritime air keeping readings in the low-to-mid 20s Celsius.

Ensemble forecasts show tight clustering around 21–23°C as the most probable range, consistent with early September climatology when unsettled patterns often cap highs despite occasional warmer intrusions. Higher outcomes above 24°C carry low implied probability due to the expected cloud and wind effects, while sub-20°C scenarios remain unlikely absent stronger cooling. Updated model runs and Met Office briefings on frontal timing will be key near-term catalysts for any shifts in these market-implied odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zggg

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent cloud cover and light precipitation expected on September 4 are capping daytime heating in Guangzhou, producing the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 28–30 °C.** Current observations show overcast skies with temperatures near 25 °C and northwest winds of 15–20 km/h under high humidity. Multiple forecast models diverge on the extent of clearing and any showers: some project a high near 23–26 °C with rain cooling the boundary layer, while others indicate partial breaks allowing readings closer to 28 °C. This spread in guidance, typical for short-range subtropical summer forecasts influenced by monsoon moisture, explains the balanced probabilities across the 28–30 °C outcomes. Traders are monitoring the next official China Meteorological Administration updates and any rapid changes in observed cloud trends ahead of the daily maximum.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=khou

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zhcc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models converge on a peak temperature near 30–31°C for Zhengzhou on September 4 under clear to mostly sunny skies and light northeasterly flow.** Official guidance and ensemble outputs indicate strong daytime heating from high pressure and minimal cloud cover, with dew points in the mid-teens Celsius supporting efficient radiational warming. Subtle differences in afternoon wind timing and any residual moisture could shift the daily maximum by 1–2°C, explaining the tight market spread between the 30°C and 31°C outcomes. Historical September climatology for the region shows typical highs near 28–30°C, so current conditions represent modest above-average warmth. Updated model runs and local observations through the overnight period will refine the exact peak before resolution.
